q: 1. On which date was the South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation (SAARC) officially established?
explain: SAARC was established on December 8, 1985, with the signing of the SAARC Charter during the 1st Summit in Dhaka, Bangladesh. May 2, 1980 is when regional cooperation was first proposed; January 16, 1987 is when the Secretariat was founded in Kathmandu; April 4, 2007 is when Afghanistan joined at the 14th Summit.

q: 2. Who is recognized as the 'Father of SAARC' for mooting the concept of regional cooperation?
explain: Ziaur Rahman mooted the regional cooperation concept in 1980 and is historically recognized as the Father of SAARC. King Birendra hosted and inaugurated the Secretariat in Kathmandu; Rajiv Gandhi was a signatory for India; Jigme Singye Wangchuck was the signatory for Bhutan.

q: 3. The official SAARC Logo was designed by which Nepalese artist?
explain: The logo, featuring two hands and seven peace doves, was designed by Shailendra Maharjan, a famous artist from Nepal. Yadav Kant Silwal was Nepal's first Secretary-General, Mahesh Acharya signed the SAPTA agreement for Nepal, and Arjun Bahadur Thapa was Nepal's second Secretary-General.

q: 4. What do the seven pigeons in the official SAARC logo represent?
explain: The seven doves nestled between the hands represent the original seven founding member countries seeking regional peace. Objectives refers to Article I (8 objectives); organs refers to the structural framework; agreements refers to trade treaties like SAPTA, SAFTA, and SATIS.

q: 5. Where is the permanent headquarters (Secretariat) of SAARC located?
explain: The permanent Secretariat was established in Kathmandu on January 16, 1987. Dhaka is where the founding summit took place; Islamabad and New Delhi host major summits and specialized bodies.

q: 6. What is the official working language of SAARC?
explain: English is the official working and administrative language of the SAARC Secretariat and all intergovernmental activities. Hindi, Nepali, and Bengali represent national languages of member countries but are not the official administrative language of SAARC.

q: 7. In which month and year was the first SAARC Summit held?
explain: The 1st Summit took place on December 7-8, 1985, in Dhaka. November 1980 is when Ziaur Rahman formally mooted the concept; April 1981 was the Foreign Secretaries meeting in Colombo; August 1983 was the Foreign Ministers meeting in New Delhi.

q: 8. Who inaugurated the SAARC Secretariat in Kathmandu on January 16, 1987?
explain: King Birendra officially inaugurated the permanent Secretariat in Kathmandu on January 16, 1987. Ziaur Rahman died prior to the inauguration; Abul Ahsan was the first Secretary-General inaugurated; King Gyanendra represented Nepal in 2005.

q: 9. What is the official motto of SAARC?
options: Deeper Integration for Peace and Prosperity
explain: This is the official motto of SAARC, emphasizing economic harmonization and peace. The other options represent generic regional cooperation phrases not officially adopted by the Charter.

q: 10. Under which Article of the United Nations Charter are regional organizations like SAARC established?
explain: Article 52 of the UN Charter permits regional arrangements to maintain international peace and security. Article 51 deals with self-defense; Article 111 is the closing article of the UN Charter; Article 19 governs voting rights.

q: 11. When did the concept of regional cooperation in South Asia first get raised by President Ziaur Rahman?
explain: President Ziaur Rahman first raised the concept on May 2, 1980. December 8, 1985 is the actual establishment date; April 11, 1993 is when SAPTA was signed; January 1, 2006 is when SAFTA entered into force.

q: 12. In which city did the Foreign Secretaries first meet in April 1981 to consult on South Asian cooperation?
explain: The Foreign Secretaries met in Colombo, Sri Lanka, in April 1981 to draft the initial areas of cooperation. New Delhi, Dhaka, and Kathmandu hosted later consultative or summit meetings.

q: 13. Where did the Foreign Ministers meet in August 1983 to launch the Integrated Programme of Action (IPA)?
explain: The Foreign Ministers met in New Delhi in August 1983, formally launching the Integrated Programme of Action (IPA) under SARC. Bangalore, Male, and Islamabad hosted subsequent summits.

q: 14. Which country was the first to propose the concept of trade liberalization (SAPTA) at the Colombo Summit in 1991?
explain: Sri Lanka first mooted trade liberalization at the 6th Summit in Colombo in December 1991. India, Nepal, and Bangladesh were co-signatories to SAPTA but not the original proposers.

q: 15. How many observer countries are currently associated with SAARC?
explain: SAARC currently has nine official observer nations (Australia, China, EU, Iran, Japan, South Korea, Mauritius, Myanmar, and USA). Seven represents the founding countries; Eight represents the current member states.

q: 16. Which country formally joined as the eighth member state of SAARC on April 4, 2007?
explain: Afghanistan became the eighth member on April 4, 2007 at the 14th Summit in New Delhi. Maldives, Bhutan, and Sri Lanka are founding member states established in 1985.

q: 17. Which of the following represents the correct count of landlocked countries in SAARC?
explain: There are three landlocked member countries in SAARC: Nepal, Bhutan, and Afghanistan. Two refers to island countries (Sri Lanka and Maldives).

q: 18. Which three SAARC member states are landlocked nations?
explain: These three are the only landlocked nations in the regional block. The other options are incorrect as they include coastal nations like Pakistan, Maldives, or Bangladesh.

q: 19. Which is the largest SAARC country by geographical area?
explain: India is the largest country with an area of 3.287 million sq km. Pakistan is the second largest; Afghanistan and Bangladesh are smaller by area rank.

q: 20. Which is the smallest SAARC country by area and population?
explain: Maldives is the smallest country by area (298 sq km) and population rank (8th). Bhutan is 7th in both area and population ranks.

q: 21. What is the geographical area of the Maldives as recorded in the SAARC country profiles?
explain: The country profile confirms Maldives' territory spans 298 sq km. 3.287 million sq km is India's area.

q: 22. Which SAARC nation has 'Shora' as the official name of its parliament?
explain: Afghanistan's parliament is known as 'Shora'. Bangladesh's is Jatiya Sangsad, Bhutan's is Tshogdu, and Maldives' is Majlis.

q: 23. What is the name of the parliament of Bangladesh?
explain: Bangladesh's unicameral parliament is called Jatiya Sangsad. Tshogdu is Bhutan's parliament, Majlis is Maldives' parliament, and Lok Sabha is India's lower house.

q: 24. Which country's parliament is known as 'Tshogdu'?
explain: Bhutan's national legislature is historically called Tshogdu. Nepal's is the National Assembly and House of Representatives; Sri Lanka has the State Assembly; Pakistan has an Assembly and Senate.

q: 25. The national animal of Bhutan is the:
explain: The Takin (Budorcas taxicolor) is the national animal of Bhutan. Bengal Tiger is Bangladesh's national animal, Markhor is Pakistan's, and Lion is Sri Lanka's.

q: 26. The parliament of the Maldives is known as:
explain: The parliament of the Maldives is called Majlis. Shora is Afghanistan's, Tshogdu is Bhutan's, and National Assembly refers to Nepal/Pakistan's lower house.

q: 27. The cow is the national animal of which SAARC country?
explain: The cow is the national animal of Nepal. India and Bangladesh have tigers as national animals; Sri Lanka has the lion.

q: 28. Which SAARC country has the Markhor as its national animal?
explain: The Markhor is the national animal of Pakistan. Afghanistan has sheep, and India has the tiger.

q: 29. What is the time difference of Bangladesh and Bhutan with Nepal?
explain: Bangladesh and Bhutan are both +15 minutes ahead of Nepal standard time. -0:15 is India and Sri Lanka; -0:45 is Pakistan and Maldives.

q: 30. Which SAARC country is at -0:15 minutes behind Nepal's local time?
explain: India and Sri Lanka are both -15 minutes behind Nepal time. Afghanistan is -1:15 behind; Pakistan and Maldives are -0:45 behind Nepal.

q: 31. How many Articles are there in the official SAARC Charter?
explain: The SAARC Charter comprises exactly ten Articles and a Preamble. Seven is the number of founding nations; Eight is the number of current members.

q: 32. Which Article of the SAARC Charter outlines the eight core objectives of the Association?
explain: Article I defines the eight core objectives of the Association. Article II defines principles, Article III defines summits, and Article IV defines the Council of Ministers.

q: 33. Which Article of the SAARC Charter details the three operational principles of cooperation?
explain: Article II defines the three operational principles of cooperation. Article V governs the Standing Committee; Article VIII governs the Secretariat.

q: 34. Which of the following is NOT one of the three principles laid down in Article II of the SAARC Charter?
options: Cooperation shall complement bilateral and multilateral frameworks
Decisions shall be taken on the basis of a simple majority
Cooperation shall not be inconsistent with bilateral and multilateral obligations
explain: Article II contains no voting provisions. Decisions under SAARC are made on the basis of consensus (unanimity), not majority. The other options are the actual principles defined in Article II.

q: 35. Which Article of the SAARC Charter governs the Summit meetings of the Heads of State or Government?
explain: Article III mandates that meetings of Heads of State or Government shall be held once every two years (Summit). Articles IV, V, and X cover other organs and general provisions.

q: 36. Which Article of the SAARC Charter defines the composition and functions of the Council of Ministers?
explain: Article IV outlines the Council of Ministers (Foreign Ministers), their duties, and bi-annual meetings. Articles III, V, and VI govern other bodies.

q: 37. The Standing Committee of Foreign Secretaries is established under which Article of the SAARC Charter?
explain: Article V establishes the Standing Committee of Foreign Secretaries. Articles IV, VI, and VII govern other committees.

q: 38. Technical Committees of SAARC are governed under which Article of the Charter?
explain: Technical Committees comprising specialists are established and regulated under Article VI. Article VII governs Action Committees.

q: 39. Which Article of the SAARC Charter governs the establishment and role of the permanent Secretariat?
explain: Article VIII establishes the administrative Secretariat and governs the role of the Secretary-General. Articles VII and IX cover other details.

q: 40. The financial arrangements and voluntary contributions of SAARC are detailed under which Article?
explain: Article IX covers financial arrangements, voluntary budget allocations, and Secretariat expenditures. Article VIII covers administration.

q: 41. General Provisions of the SAARC Charter are outlined in which Article?
explain: Article X contains the General Provisions, including consensus rules and bilateral exclusion. Articles IV and IX cover ministers and finance.

q: 42. How many core objectives are defined under Article I of the SAARC Charter?
explain: Article I contains exactly 8 specific objectives. Three is the number of principles; Seven is the number of founding states.

q: 43. How many core principles of cooperation are defined under Article II of the SAARC Charter?
explain: Article II contains exactly three core operational principles. Five refers to specialized bodies; Ten refers to Articles.

q: 44. Which of the following is a primary objective of SAARC under Article I?
options: To establish a common military defense pact
To promote the welfare of the peoples of South Asia and improve their quality of life
To enforce a single currency across South Asia
To merge the administrative ministries of member states
explain: This is the first and primary objective under Article I. The other options are military/currency items not in the Charter.

q: 45. Which of the following is an operational principle of SAARC under Article II?
options: Bilateral disputes shall be resolved by a majority vote
Cooperation shall substitute bilateral and multilateral cooperation
Cooperation shall be based on respect for sovereign equality and territorial integrity
Working language shall rotate among the member capitals
explain: This is the first principle under Article II. Bilateral disputes are excluded from the Charter; cooperation complements, not substitutes, bilateral frameworks.

q: 46. Who was the first Secretary-General of SAARC?
explain: Abul Ahsan of Bangladesh was appointed the first Secretary-General, serving from 1987 to 1989. Yadav Kant Silwal was 4th, Kant Kishore Bhargava was 2nd, and Ibrahim Hussein Zaki was 3rd.

q: 47. Which country's representative was the first Secretary-General of SAARC?
explain: The first SG, Abul Ahsan, represented Bangladesh. India, Pakistan, and Nepal contributed Secretaries-General at a later stage.

q: 48. Who was the first person from Nepal to serve as the Secretary-General of SAARC?
explain: Yadav Kant Silwal was the first person from Nepal, serving as the 4th SG (1994-1995). Arjun Bahadur Thapa was the second person from Nepal.

q: 49. Who was the second person from Nepal to serve as the Secretary-General of SAARC?
explain: Arjun Bahadur Thapa was the second person from Nepal, serving as the 12th SG (2014-2017). Yadav Kant Silwal was the first; Dr. Bhesh Bahadur Thapa was a signatory to SAFTA.

q: 50. What is the tenure of the SAARC Secretary-General as decided at the Ninth Summit?
explain: The Ninth Summit extended the SG's tenure from two to three years. The other options are incorrect based on current rules.
